problem: LLM-based embodied task planners are stateless and reactive: they lose short-term context within an episode (e.g. toggling a faucet repeatedly) and cannot accumulate experience across tasks. Prior memory systems (e.g. RoboMemory) mostly store successful trajectories and lack task-specific working memory and systematic reflection on failures.
motivation: Long-horizon embodied tasks need both immediate situational awareness and accumulated experience. Human cognition uses working, episodic and semantic memory operating at different timescales and evolving with feedback. The paper maps this hierarchy onto a training-free memory module that plugs into arbitrary MLLM planners.
key_idea: A training-free, brain-inspired hierarchical memory (working window, episodic trajectory and spatial KGs, LLM-distilled semantic guidelines with utility-based pruning) is updated online and after each episode by an independent experience agent, and retrieved into the planner prompt.
insight: Every tier adds gains in the ablation on the EB-ALFRED base set with GPT-4o: 64.0 with no memory, 68.0 with working memory, 70.0 adding episodic, 76.0 adding semantic, and 82.0 with feedback/evolving updates. Semantic memory and the feedback/evolving mechanism give the largest jumps. Within semantic memory, removing learning insights hurts most (82.0 to 72.0), and the working-memory consistency check matters (82.0 to 70.0). Error analysis shows failures drop from 131 to 75, with procedural and action errors shrinking, while incorrect-termination errors remain.
method: Working Memory: a sliding window (default 5) of [Action, Feedback, Agent state, Location, Timestamp], with success-rate and consistency-check warnings, serialized as text into the prompt.

Episodic Memory (Trajectory KG): directed graph of state nodes and action-transition edges for completed attempts (both success and failure), storing instruction, action sequence, success, room; merged across episodes and retrieved by similarity.
Episodic Memory (Spatial KG): room-contains-object and object near/on/in object relations, retrieved for the same room and accumulated across episodes.

Semantic Memory: after each episode an Experience Agent (LLM) distills success patterns, failure causes and learning insights into guidelines; a utility score (0.7*confidence + 0.3*usage, with decay and pruning, max M=20) keeps them compact; top-k (k=2) retrieved by task type and object category.
Guided-retry: failed episodes are retried with real-time feedback up to a limit to enrich semantic memory; success is counted only on the first attempt.

Hierarchical retrieval and evolution: the query (room, task type, object) pulls from all tiers into a prompt; step-level updates (working memory, trajectory KG, spatial KG) and episode-level updates (finalize KGs, LLM summarization, guideline update/pruning).

setting.backbone: Frozen MLLM planners: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro (plus Qwen2.5-VL-72B for the memory-method comparison); the experience agent is also an LLM
setting.training_data: none (training-free); memory is built online from the agent's own interaction history
setting.observation: 500x500 egocentric RGB images plus textual feedback/object info
setting.action_space: EmbodiedBench high-level actions (find/pick up/put down etc.) for ALFRED/Habitat, and low-level discrete navigation/manipulation actions
setting.privileged: none (memory built from the agent's own trajectories; guided-retry uses environment feedback on failed episodes)

numbers.extra: training-free memory that evolves online; step limit 30; guided retry only for memory learning

results: BrainMem lifts EB-ALFRED average SR to about 75% for GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Gemini-1.5-Pro. GPT-4o with BrainMem gains +18.7 on EB-ALFRED (56.3 to 75.0), +13.3 on EB-Navigation (57.7 to 71.0) and +18.0 on EB-Manipulation (28.9 to 46.9), and Claude-3.5-Sonnet reaches 73.0 on EB-Habitat. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B it beats the strongest memory baseline RoboMemory (75.0/82.2 vs 70.5/79.7 SR/GC average), at about 1.4x token cost.
limitations: Evaluated only on the AI2-THOR-based EmbodiedBench simulators with proprietary planners; no real robot and no full open-source-model results with BrainMem in the main tables.
Remaining failures are dominated by incorrect termination and goal inference (29% of failures), which memory does not fix.
Adds about 1.4x token overhead, and the guided-retry and LLM summarization need extra interaction and sequential episodes.
